title: RAYE Announces One-Night Orchestral Show at Royal Albert Hall
excerpt: RAYE will return to London's Royal Albert Hall on October 23 to perform her second album, *THIS MUSIC MAY CONTAIN HOPE.*, in full with the Heritage Orchestra and Flames Collective.
body:
RAYE will return to London's Royal Albert Hall on October 23 to perform her second album, *THIS MUSIC MAY CONTAIN HOPE.*, in full with the Heritage Orchestra and Flames Collective. The one-night concert is called *THIS SYMPHONY MAY CONTAIN HOPE.* and will feature her touring band alongside the orchestra and choir. The singer recorded her first orchestral concert at the same venue three years ago, but this performance will be devoted to songs she released in March.

The album is arranged as four seasons, with its music tracing a path from darker experiences toward hope. Rather than rearranging a few singles for strings, RAYE plans to perform the complete record in order. That gives the orchestra a more substantial role than providing accompaniment for the biggest choruses. The songs range from intimate passages to jazz and big-band arrangements, and the concert will have to accommodate all of them. The announcement has not specified whether the new arrangements will be recorded or released.

Her first symphonic concert took place in 2023, when she performed *My 21st Century Blues* with a 50-piece orchestra and choir. The show was filmed for *Live at the Royal Albert Hall*, which later earned a Grammy nomination for Best Music Film. She reunited with the Heritage Orchestra and Flames Collective for another symphonic performance at London's O2 the following year. This month's concert reunites those musicians for a different album, one that already makes extensive use of live instrumentation.

RAYE has also released an Abbey Road Studios performance of "I Will Overcome." recorded with the London Symphony Orchestra. The recording is separate from the forthcoming concert, which will feature the Heritage Orchestra, but it shows how the newer material sounds with a large ensemble. The song arrives early in the album, as its narrator tries to find a way through a difficult period. Here, the orchestral accompaniment gives the vocal more space without changing the song's subject.

[youtube:Iy2FoVeIUXs]

The Royal Albert Hall announcement follows six sold-out dates at London's O2 earlier this year and a North American tour. RAYE is now appearing as a guest on Bruno Mars' stadium shows. Those performances have drawn on songs from different periods of her career, whereas the new London date has a single purpose. She has chosen to present the album as one continuous performance rather than build the evening around a selection of hits.

The concert is a chance to hear the album's less familiar songs alongside its singles. RAYE has kept quieter pieces and elaborate arrangements on the same record, and the whole-album format means neither can simply be left out. The choice follows the earlier symphonic shows, but this time the music was written with the sort of instrumentation that will be onstage with her. It should be an interesting test of how the album holds together in a single live performance.

Three years ago, the Royal Albert Hall concert captured RAYE performing songs from her debut album as an independent artist. The resulting film allowed a one-night show to reach people who never had a ticket. Nothing comparable has been announced for *THIS SYMPHONY MAY CONTAIN HOPE.* yet. For now, the newly released Abbey Road performance is the only confirmed glimpse of the orchestral arrangements, while the full album performance remains planned for October 23.
